# Unichrono

> A world clock app for Android and iPhone, built around home-screen widgets
> that show several cities at once. Free on both platforms. Works entirely
> offline: no accounts, no analytics, no network calls of its own.

Unichrono is published by Spiny Valley Labs. It exists because most world
clock widgets eventually freeze: they redraw the time using background work,
and Android's battery optimisation, Doze, and the task killers that ship on
many phones shut that work down. The widget then shows a wrong time with no
indication anything is wrong. Unichrono runs nothing in the background. Each
widget reads the phone's own clock with a timezone attached, so it cannot
freeze, cannot drift, and costs no battery.

## Facts

- Platforms: Android 8.0 and later; iPhone and iPad on iOS 17 and later.
- Price: free on Android, permanently, with no paywall and no ads. Free on
  iPhone, where an optional one-time Pro unlock exists and is currently given
  away from inside the app.
- Cities: 34,804, bundled in the app rather than fetched, from GeoNames
  (CC BY 4.0).
- Widget styles: nine, including a full city list, a single hero city, three
  cities at a glance, meeting availability, sunrise and sunset, and an analog
  face. The analog widget needs Android 12 or later.
- Data: cities, labels, widget setups and alerts are stored on the device and
  deleted with the app. Nothing is collected or transmitted.
- Timezones and DST come from the database that ships with the operating
  system, so they update with it.

## Features

- Home-screen and Lock Screen widgets showing several cities at once.
- Time travel: drag a ruler and every city re-bases to that moment.
- A plan board for alarms and meetings, showing one instant in every city, and
  handing it to the phone's alarm, a calendar event, or a share sheet.
- City alerts: a notification, a vibration and a spoken line at a time you
  choose in another city's clock.
- A time announcer that speaks the local time hourly or once a day.
- An optional ongoing notification showing the clocks while other apps are open.

## Pages

- [Home](https://unichrono.app/): what the app does, with live demonstrations.
- [User guide](https://unichrono.app/help.html): every feature explained, a
  settings reference for both platforms, and troubleshooting for the common
  failures.
- [About](https://unichrono.app/about.html): why the app exists and what it
  deliberately refuses to do.
- [Privacy policy](https://unichrono.app/privacy-policy.html): what is stored,
  what is asked for, and the one thing that can leave the device.
